title: Handel’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Handel’s Missing Symphony (work id handel-symphony-1)

Honest counterfactual: Handel wrote no symphony. His orchestral music is the concerti grossi, the organ concertos, the overtures to operas and oratorios, and the outdoor suites (Water Music, Fireworks Music). This work imagines a four-movement Sinfonia in F major in that manner. It is new music; no theme is taken from Handel.

Instrumentation (11 staves, sounding pitch): 2 natural horns in F (harmonic series of F only), 2 oboes, bassoon, violins I and II, violas, cellos, double basses, harpsichord.

Movements
I. Largo – Allegro, F major: eight stately bars, then an Italian ritornello movement. An eight-bar ritornello for the full band returns in C, in D minor and in F; between its returns come episodes for two oboes and bassoon, for the first violins in running arpeggios, and for the horns answered by the oboes.
II. Larghetto, D minor, 3/4: a sarabande-like air for strings with a solo oboe in the second half.
III. Alla Hornpipe, F major, 3/2: syncopated tune for the full band with horns, a quiet D minor middle for strings, and the hornpipe again.
IV. Chaconne, F major, 3/4: variations on a four-bar ground bass (F E D C B flat B C), with a group of variations in F minor.

To differ from the Bach symphony in this batch (a French-overture suite with fugues), this one has no fugue: it is built on ritornello, song, dance and variation. Target length about ten minutes. Compromise known from the start: themes, episodes, horn parts, basses of the slow movement and the chord of every beat are written by hand; filling parts, motor basses, the harpsichord and some arpeggio figuration are realised by a program from that chord plan.

First complete draft: added the D minor Larghetto (strings, then solo oboe), the Hornpipe in 3/2 with its quiet middle section, and the Chaconne of seventeen variations on a four-bar ground. A revision pass follows.
